Like the title says, I just finished the series Mononoke. There will be spoilers, but I'll put those a little further down, after I sell you all on this anime :P

For those of you who have never heard of it, Mononoke is probably the closest thing to horror in anime that I've come across. And when I say horror, I don't mean gore, I mean horror.

To explain Mononoke's take on horror, I have to explain the structure of the show. The show follows Kusuriuri/The Medicine Seller, who travels around exorcising mononoke. Mononoke are the combination of Ayakashi (a sort of spirit) and the bad emotions and ill karma of human beings. In essence, they're almost like ghosts who can't pass on from the living world. Kusuriuri slays mononoke using a sacred sword, which can only be unsheathed if he learns the shape, truth, and reason of the mononoke. The shape is the form or name of the mononoke. The truth is how it came to be. The reason is what the mononoke is trying to achieve by its actions.

Using this premise, Mononoke creates intriguing scenarios where Kusuriuri has to use a few tools, but mostly his wits, to uncover the shape, truth, and reason of various mononoke. Mononoke is split up into several two to three episode arcs, which are more or less separate from each other. Each arc deals with a different issue, all of which have an amount of gravitas, and the show explores the human condition and the nature of evil. I describe Mononoke as horror because, in each scenario, the characters are thrust into terrifying situations, and often have to confront bizarrre phenomena at the hands of mononoke, as well as the depths of their own souls. Each arc is disturbing in its own way, but each is an incredibly enthralling ride, where nothing is as it first seems.

As a side note, I really enjoyed the art in this series. It doesn't look like a traditional anime, but more like something out of a fedual Japanese painting. I could see it being offputting to people, but I'll wager it's quick to get used to. So don't give up just because you don't like how it looks! Give it a few episodes before passing judegement.

BEWARE: There may be spoilers from here on!

Alright, so down to the discussion. I promise this won't be as long as my pitch! I have one main thing want to discuss with those of you who've seen Mononoke: What do you think this show is trying to say about the nature of evil and its connection with the human condition?

In each arc, the mononoke don't seem to be the ones at fault. Often, they are the result of the wickedness of others, and simply want justice for those who did them wrong. However, Kusuriuri slays each and every one of them without hesitation. His purpose is to slay mononoke, and he does so without hesitation. Why can mononoke not be allowed to exist? Is justice for the wronged a bad thing? Is Kusuriuri actually freeing the mononoke, rather than slaying them? It seems as though the perpetrators sometimes escape unscathed. But is the torture of the experience the punishment itself? Basically, my question is: Is Kusuriuri a dealer of justice or a single-minded machine that exists solely to slay mononoke without question?

I'd also love to hear anyone's thoughts on how Kusuriuri seems to be an ever-persisting presence in the human world. What might he represent, if anything? Does he only exist to highlight the fact that evil, too, will always be a part of being human?
[SPOILERS] Just finished Mononoke; would like to [RECOMMEND]/[DISCUSS] with everyone!
